easy.def: A thing with parts that does a job.
examples: A washing machine cleans our clothes.
This machine makes ice.
The machine is very loud.

more.def: A piece of equipment with moving parts that uses power to do work.
examples: The machine at the factory fills a hundred bottles every minute.
A machine at the bank counts the coins.
The farmer uses a machine to pick the corn.

easy.def: Feeling angry.
examples: I was mad when my tower fell.
She is mad at her brother.
The cat looked mad.

more.def: Feeling or showing anger.
examples: He was mad because his little brother broke his model.
She got mad when the game ended early.
The coach was mad about the missed practice.

easy.def: A polite way to speak to a woman.
examples: Yes, madam.
Can I help you, madam?
Welcome, madam.

more.def: A polite word used when speaking to a woman.
examples: "May I help you, madam?" asked the clerk.
The waiter said, "Right this way, madam."
"Thank you, madam," said the boy.

easy.def: A book with pictures and stories that comes out each week or month.
examples: I read a magazine.
The magazine has pictures.
A new magazine came.

more.def: A thin book with articles and pictures that is printed every week or month.
examples: Mom reads a cooking magazine.
The magazine has a story about owls.
A new issue of my magazine came in the mail.

easy.def: Tricks or powers that seem impossible.
examples: The wizard used magic.
The magician did magic.
The story has magic in it.

more.def: Special powers or clever tricks that seem to break the rules of nature.
examples: In the story, the wizard uses magic to make a castle.
The magician amazed us with card magic.
There is a touch of magic in the winter woods.

easy.def: Having special powers.
examples: She has a magic wand.
The magic hat made a rabbit appear.
They found a magic bean.

more.def: Having special powers that seem impossible.
examples: The fairy waved her magic wand.
In the tale, a magic mirror speaks.
He planted a magic bean that grew into a huge tree.

easy.def: A thing that pulls some metal to it.
examples: The magnet stuck to the fridge.
A magnet can pick up a nail.
The magnet holds my drawing up.

more.def: A piece of metal or rock that pulls iron and steel toward it.
examples: We used a magnet to pick up the spilled pins.
A compass needle is a small magnet.
The two magnets snapped together.

easy.def: Very, very beautiful or great.
examples: The fireworks were magnificent!
The king had a magnificent crown.
What a magnificent rainbow!

more.def: Extremely beautiful, grand, or impressive.
examples: From the top of the mountain, the view was magnificent.
The peacock spread its magnificent tail.
The palace has a magnificent hall with gold walls.

easy.def: Letters and packages that are sent.
examples: The mail came.
I got mail.
Check the mail.

more.def: Letters, cards and packages that are sent through the post office.
examples: The mail came before lunch.
I got a card in the mail.
We check the mail every afternoon.

easy.def: To send by mail.
examples: Mail the letter.
I mailed a card.
She mails packages.

more.def: To send a letter or package through the post office.
examples: I mailed a card to my grandmother.
Dad mailed the package on Monday.
She mails letters every week.

easy.def: Most important.
examples: The main road is busy.
The main part of the story.
The main door.

more.def: Most important or largest of its kind.
examples: The main road goes through the middle of town.
The main character of the book is a dog.
Use the main door at the front of the school.

easy.def: A title used for a king or queen.
examples: Your Majesty.
His Majesty the king.
Her Majesty the queen.

more.def: A title of respect for a king or queen.
examples: "Your Majesty," said the knight, "the dragon is gone."
The people bowed before Her Majesty.
His Majesty welcomed the visitors.

easy.def: Very big or important.
examples: It was a major storm.
He has a major part in the play.
A major road is near.

more.def: Larger or more important than others of its kind.
examples: The city built a major bridge over the river.
Pollution is a major problem for rivers.
She had a major role in the school play.

easy.def: To put things together to get something new.
examples: I make a card.
She made a cake.
We make a fort.

more.def: To build, create, or prepare something by putting parts together.
examples: Bees make honey from the nectar of flowers.
We made a poster for the school play.
He is making a sandwich for his lunch.

easy.def: To cause something to happen.
examples: The joke made me laugh.
Rain makes puddles.
She made him smile.

more.def: To cause something to happen or to be a certain way.
examples: The loud thunder made the baby cry.
Good exercise makes your body strong.
Sunlight makes the plants grow tall.

easy.def: Being the kind that does not lay eggs or have babies.
examples: A male lion has a mane.
The male bird has bright feathers.
A male dog.

more.def: Of the kind of animal or person that does not have babies.
examples: A male lion has a thick mane.
The male peacock has bright tail feathers.
A male and a female dog played together.

easy.def: A man, boy or he-animal.
examples: The male has stripes.
A male was in the cage.
The male is larger.

more.def: A man, a boy or an animal that is not able to have babies.
examples: The male of the species is bigger.
Two males fought over the food.
The male guards the nest.

easy.def: A name for your mother.
examples: Mama made soup.
I love my mama.
The baby called, "Mama!"

more.def: A word that young children use for their mother.
examples: The baby reached for her mama.
"Mama, look at my drawing!" shouted the boy.
My mama sings while she cooks.

easy.def: An animal with fur or hair that feeds milk to its babies.
examples: A dog is a mammal.
A cat is a mammal.
People are mammals too.

more.def: A warm-blooded animal that has hair or fur and feeds its babies with milk.
examples: Whales are mammals, even though they live in the sea.
Bats are the only mammals that can fly.
Like all mammals, a baby elephant drinks its mother's milk.

easy.def: A male person who is not a child.
examples: The man waved to us.
A man fixed our car.
That man is my uncle.

more.def: An adult male person.
examples: The man at the bakery gave us warm bread.
Two men carried the piano up the stairs.
He grew from a small boy into a tall man.

easy.def: To be able to do something hard.
examples: I managed to climb the hill.
She managed to lift the box.
We managed to finish.

more.def: To succeed in doing something that is hard.
examples: I managed to climb to the top of the hill.
She managed to lift the heavy box.
We managed to finish before dark.

easy.def: To be in charge of.
examples: She manages the shop.
He manages the team.
Mom manages the office.

more.def: To be in charge of a business, place or group.
examples: She manages the bookshop on Main Street.
He manages the swim team.
Mom manages a busy office.

easy.def: A person in charge of a shop or team.
examples: The manager of the shop is nice.
The manager helped us.
The team manager spoke.

more.def: A person whose job is to be in charge of a shop, team or business.
examples: The manager of the toy store helped us find a gift.
The baseball manager chose the team.
The manager told the workers to take a break.

easy.def: A large number of.
examples: I have many toys.
Many birds fly south.
How many are there?

more.def: A large number of people or things.
examples: Many students ride the bus to school.
There are too many stars in the sky to count.
How many apples are in the basket?

easy.def: A drawing that shows places.
examples: The map shows the way.
I read the map.
The map has roads.

more.def: A drawing that shows where places are.
examples: The map shows where our school is.
We used a map to find the trail.
The map of the world has seven continents.

easy.def: The third month of the year.
examples: Spring begins in March.
My birthday is in March.
March can be very windy.

more.def: The third month of the year, when spring begins in many places.
examples: The cherry trees bloom in March.
Strong winds lift kites into the sky in March.
March comes after February and before April.

easy.def: To walk with steady steps.
examples: We march in a line to lunch.
Ants march across the sidewalk.
The band marched down the street.

more.def: To walk with regular, steady steps, often in a group.
examples: The band marched through the town during the parade.
Hundreds of penguins march across the ice together.
The kindergarten class marched around the playground.

easy.def: A place where people buy and sell things.
examples: We went to the market.
The market sells fruit.
The farmers' market is busy.

more.def: A place where people buy and sell goods, often outdoors.
examples: We buy vegetables at the farmers' market.
The market was full of colorful fruit.
Fish are sold at the market by the harbor.

easy.def: The time when two people are husband and wife.
examples: Their marriage is happy.
Grandma and Grandpa had a long marriage.
The marriage began in a garden.

more.def: The state of being married to someone.
examples: My grandparents celebrated fifty years of marriage.
Their marriage was a happy one.
The marriage ceremony took place in a garden.

easy.def: Joined together as a husband and wife.
examples: My aunt is married.
They are a married pair.
The married couple smiled.

more.def: Having a husband or a wife by a wedding.
examples: My parents have been married for fifteen years.
The newly married couple waved from the car.
Her uncle is married to my teacher.

easy.def: To become husband and wife.
examples: My aunt will marry in June.
They married last year.
Two people marry at a wedding.

more.def: To join with someone as a husband or wife in a special ceremony.
examples: My cousin is going to marry her best friend next summer.
They married in a garden full of flowers.
Many people marry in the spring.

easy.def: Someone who is very good at something.
examples: He is a master painter.
The master carved the bowl.
He is a chess master.

more.def: A person who has great skill at something.
examples: The master baker made the wedding cake.
She is a master of the violin.
A master carver made the wooden horse.

easy.def: To learn something very well.
examples: I mastered tying my shoes.
She mastered the piano piece.
He mastered the trick.

more.def: To learn something so well that you can do it easily.
examples: It took a year to master the violin.
She mastered riding a bike without help.
He mastered the card trick after hours of practice.

easy.def: A thin stick that makes fire.
examples: A grown-up lit a match.
The match went out.
The box of matches is on the shelf.

more.def: A small stick with a tip that makes a flame when rubbed on a rough surface.
examples: Dad struck a match to light the candle.
A box of matches sat on the shelf.
He blew out the match.

easy.def: A game between teams.
examples: We watched the soccer match.
The tennis match was long.
My dad won his tennis match.

more.def: A contest between two players or teams.
examples: The tennis match lasted two hours.
Our team won the match.
She watched the chess match.

easy.def: To go together.
examples: The socks match.
Her shoes match her dress.
These two colors match.

more.def: To be alike or to go well together.
examples: Her scarf matches her hat.
Match each word with its picture.
The two socks match.

related.def: Things that do not go together.

easy.def: A friend or partner.
examples: My mate and I play.
The ship's mate.
A classmate.

more.def: A friend or a partner, or a person you share something with.
examples: My teammate and I passed the ball.
The ship's mate told the crew what to do.
My roommate and I share a room.

easy.def: An animal's partner.
examples: The bird found a mate.
Wolves have one mate.
The swan stays with its mate.

more.def: One of a pair of animals that come together to have young.
examples: The bird sang to find a mate.
Swans stay with the same mate for life.
The wolf stayed close to its mate.

easy.def: To be important.
examples: You matter to me.
It does not matter.
What matters is being kind.

more.def: To be important or to make a difference.
examples: It does not matter who wins, as long as we have fun.
Your opinion matters to our class.
Good sleep matters when you are growing.

easy.def: What things are made of.
examples: Rock is a kind of matter.
Water is matter.
Air is matter too.

more.def: Anything that takes up space and has weight, such as solids, liquids, and gases.
examples: Rocks, water, and air are all kinds of matter.
Matter can change from ice to water to steam.
Scientists study how matter behaves when it is heated.

easy.def: A word used to ask or say what is allowed.
examples: May I go out?
You may sit here.
May I have some?

more.def: A word used to ask for permission, or to say that something is possible.
examples: May I borrow your ruler for a minute?
It may rain later, so take an umbrella.
You may leave the table when you have finished eating.

easy.def: Not sure, but it may be.
examples: Maybe it will rain.
Maybe I can come.
Maybe she is home.

more.def: Possibly, or perhaps, when you are not sure.
examples: Maybe we can go to the park if the rain stops.
I am not sure, but maybe my sister took it.
Maybe the answer is on the next page.

easy.def: The leader of a city or town.
examples: The mayor spoke.
Our mayor is kind.
The mayor cut the ribbon.

more.def: The leader of a city or town, chosen by the people who live there.
examples: The mayor cut the ribbon at the new park.
Our mayor visited the school.
The mayor gave a speech at the parade.
